PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 31% chance, and it went the way we feared.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 69% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Philadelphia’s power play hit a new low
surprises.body: Philadelphia has had one of the league’s least effective power plays, and Carolina has had one of the league’s best penalty kills for years. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Philadelphia’s power play created 1.4 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.5 (about 6.8 against Carolina) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Philadelphia couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Carolina usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: Philadelphia’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% (about 7.0% against Carolina) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Carolina hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Carolina usually hits more than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 62 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 116 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: The Hurricanes take down the Flyers
paras: Andrei Svechnikov and Shayne Gostisbehere scored 3:29 apart midway through the second to put the Hurricanes up 2-0. Christian Dvorak got the Flyers on the board 1:41 later. Sebastian Aho made it 3-1 for the Hurricanes 1:28 later. Mark Jankowski stretched the lead to 4-1 with 4:51 left.

The Hurricanes drove the play, outshooting the Flyers 30-19, and the scoreboard caught up. Pyotr Kochetkov made 18 saves for the Hurricanes, and Joseph Woll stopped 26 of 30. The Canes moved to 5-1-1.

items.text: The Flyers are 0-5-2, still looking for their first win.
Trevor Zegras’s six-game point streak against Carolina ended.
